rationale: No record changes in this pass; the index offers no open question, gap or source relationship whose resolution would alter a judgment. What the audit leaves behind, including where each main account could be reopened, is this. The asserted defect is the witness flag in the per-cluster summary: stored by the configuration-change notification, dropped by the rebuild, false on both caller-visible branches, on a documented query surface, and with no in-tree consumer, so it is a reporting defect on a client contract and not a consensus one; it would have to be reopened if a caller were found that reads the field for a decision, or if the field description were changed to disclaim the role. The snapshot save and worker panic accounts now rest on a documented halting requirement plus a launcher execution, and would reopen if the pinned launcher were changed to recover panics or if an engine worker were observed surviving a panic. The snapshot install, restart, apply ordering and vote durability accounts are source- or object-level and would reopen on a live-follower execution that shows a different frontier, or on a storage layer whose write batch can return before durability. The witness eligibility accounts are anchored in the configuration contract and would reopen on a change to how quorum membership is computed. The read, configuration-change and snapshot refusal paths are consistent because every client entry point rejects a witness before request state exists, and would reopen if a caller reached a node path that skips those admission checks. No further record is proposed because none of those conditions is present in the captured tree.
